questions.stem: Agriculture provides employment in Nigeria mainly because
options: it needs no human labour at all
many people earn a living as farmers, processors and sellers of farm produce
it is practised only by government workers
it is carried out only in big cities
questions.explanation: Farming, processing, transporting and selling farm produce give jobs to millions of Nigerians, so agriculture is the largest employer of labour.

questions.stem: The keeping of fish in ponds or tanks for food and sale is called
questions.explanation: Aquaculture is the rearing of fish and other water organisms under controlled conditions such as ponds and tanks.

questions.stem: Farming in which a farmer produces mainly enough food to feed his own family is called
questions.explanation: A subsistence farmer produces mainly for household consumption, with little or nothing left for sale.

questions.stem: Timber, bamboo and grass for thatch, obtained from farms and forests, show that agriculture provides
questions.explanation: Timber, bamboo and thatch are used to build houses and roofs, so agriculture supplies materials for shelter.

questions.stem: The growing of fruits, vegetables and flowers such as oranges, tomatoes and roses is called
questions.explanation: Horticulture is the branch of crop growing that deals with fruits, vegetables and ornamental plants such as flowers.

questions.stem: Mr Okoro grows only cocoa on a very large estate in Ondo State and sells all the beans to processors. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Growing a single cash crop on a large estate for sale is plantation farming, which is common for cocoa, oil palm and rubber.

questions.stem: Which of the following products is obtained from apiculture?
questions.explanation: Apiculture is bee keeping, and the main products of bees are honey and beeswax.

questions.stem: Snail rearing is becoming popular in southern Nigeria mainly because snails
options: are useful as guard animals on the farm
can be used to plough the land
need little space and their meat is rich in protein
questions.explanation: Snails can be raised in small pens with cheap feed such as leaves and fruits, and snail meat is high in protein, so it is a profitable small business.

questions.stem: A farmer leaves a piece of farmland to rest for some years so that it regains its fertility, then returns to farm it again. This practice is called
questions.explanation: In bush fallowing, the land is left uncultivated for some years so that natural vegetation restores soil fertility before it is farmed again.

questions.stem: Herders in northern Nigeria who move their cattle southwards during the dry season and return north in the rainy season are practising
questions.explanation: Transhumance is the seasonal movement of herders and their livestock between areas in search of pasture and water.

questions.stem: The Adeyemi family in Ibadan keeps 200 layers and 50 snails and also grows vegetables behind their house. Which form of agricultural activity is NOT practised by the family?
questions.explanation: Layers are poultry, snails show snail rearing and vegetables show crop growing; the family keeps no bees, so apiculture is not practised.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST reason why government encourages young people in Nigeria to take up farming?
options: To increase the importation of food
To reduce unemployment and increase food supply
To reduce the number of farm produce markets
To stop the growth of agro-based industries
questions.explanation: More young people in farming creates jobs and raises food production, reducing hunger and the need to import food.

questions.stem: Crops that take two years or two growing seasons to complete their life cycle are called
questions.explanation: Biennial crops grow vegetatively in the first season and complete flowering and seed production in the second.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a fibre crop?
questions.explanation: Cotton is grown mainly for its lint fibres, which are spun into thread and woven into cloth.

questions.stem: Fluted pumpkin (ugu) and amaranthus (green) are grown mainly as
questions.explanation: The leaves of ugu and amaranthus are cooked as vegetables in soups and stews, so they are leafy vegetable crops.

questions.stem: Yam, cocoyam and sweet potato are grouped together as
questions.explanation: These crops store food in underground roots, tubers or corms, so they are classed as root and tuber crops.

questions.stem: Which group of crops is grown mainly for its oil?
questions.explanation: Oil is extracted from palm fruits, groundnut seeds and sesame (beniseed), so these are oil crops.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a beverage crop?
questions.explanation: Coffee beans are roasted and ground to make a drink, so coffee is a beverage crop like cocoa and tea.

questions.stem: Which of the following features is found in monocotyledonous crops?
questions.explanation: Monocots such as maize and rice have parallel-veined leaves and fibrous roots; net veins, taproots and two cotyledons belong to dicots.

questions.stem: Which group contains only monocotyledonous crops?
questions.explanation: Rice, millet and sugarcane are grasses with one seed leaf; cowpea, groundnut, soya bean, melon, okra and pumpkin are dicots.

questions.stem: Ginger grown in southern Kaduna State is classified as a
questions.explanation: Ginger rhizomes are used to add flavour to food and drinks, so ginger is a spice crop.

questions.stem: The rubber tree is grown mainly for its
questions.explanation: The rubber tree is tapped for latex, a milky fluid processed into rubber for tyres, foam and gloves.

questions.stem: Pawpaw, mango and guava are classified as
questions.explanation: These crops are grown for their edible fruits, which are rich in vitamins.

questions.stem: Elephant grass and guinea grass grown to feed cattle and goats are called
questions.explanation: Grasses and legumes grown for livestock to graze or to be cut and fed to them are forage or pasture crops.

questions.stem: Which pair of crops are BOTH perennial?
questions.explanation: Cocoa and oil palm live and produce for many years; maize and cowpea complete their life cycle in one season.

questions.stem: Which crop is a good source of BOTH protein and oil?
questions.explanation: Groundnut seeds contain a high level of oil and also much protein; cassava and yam mainly supply carbohydrate and orange supplies vitamins.

questions.stem: Which of the following crops is correctly matched with its main use?
questions.explanation: Kenaf is grown for fibre used to make sacks and ropes; ginger is a spice, rubber gives latex and cotton gives fibre.

questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals
questions.stem: Cattle reared mainly for meat are called
questions.explanation: Beef cattle are kept mainly for meat production, while dairy cattle are kept for milk.

questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals
questions.stem: Which of these is a poultry bird?
questions.explanation: Poultry are domestic birds such as chickens, ducks, turkeys and guinea fowl; rabbits and grasscutters are mammals and snails are molluscs.

questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals
questions.stem: Animals kept at home mainly for companionship and pleasure are called
questions.explanation: Pets such as cats and dogs are kept mainly for companionship and enjoyment.

questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals
questions.stem: Which of the following is an aquatic farm animal?
questions.explanation: Aquatic animals live in water; catfish are reared in ponds, while goats, rabbits and turkeys live on land.

questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals
questions.stem: Which farm animal is reared for wool?
questions.explanation: Sheep produce wool, which is sheared and spun into yarn, as well as meat.

questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals
questions.stem: Farm animals that give birth to their young and feed them with milk are called
questions.explanation: Mammals have hair and mammary glands that produce milk for their young; goats, cattle and pigs are examples.

questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals
questions.stem: When a ruminant is said to chew the cud, it means that it
options: brings swallowed food back to the mouth and chews it again
swallows stones to grind its food
eats only grains and no grass
chews food only once before swallowing
questions.explanation: Ruminants swallow grass quickly, then return it from the rumen to the mouth to chew again, which helps them digest fibre.

questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals
questions.stem: Goats, sheep and cattle are classified by habitat as
questions.explanation: These animals live and feed on land, so by habitat they are terrestrial.

questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals
questions.stem: Poultry birds differ from farm mammals because they
questions.explanation: Birds have feathers and reproduce by laying eggs, while mammals have hair, give birth to live young and produce milk.

questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals
questions.stem: Chickens reared mainly for egg production are called
questions.explanation: Layers are hens bred and kept for egg production; broilers are raised for meat.

questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals
questions.stem: Which work animal is well suited to the dry areas of far north-eastern Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Camels can go for long periods without water and walk well on sand, so they are used for carrying loads in dry areas like Borno.

questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals
questions.stem: Which group contains only monogastric animals?
questions.explanation: Pigs, chickens and rabbits have a simple stomach, while goats, sheep and cattle are ruminants with four stomach compartments.

questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals
questions.stem: Which breed of cattle is well known for its tolerance to trypanosomiasis in the humid south of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: N'Dama cattle are trypanotolerant, so they survive in tsetse-infested humid areas where large zebu breeds such as White Fulani and Red Bororo suffer.

questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals
questions.stem: The West African Dwarf goat is common in southern Nigeria mainly because it
options: tolerates the hot, humid climate and local diseases
questions.explanation: The West African Dwarf goat is small, hardy and adapted to the humid forest zone and its diseases, so farmers there keep it easily.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Weeds reduce crop yield mainly because they
options: compete with crops for water, nutrients, light and space
add nutrients to the soil for crops
questions.explanation: Weeds grow alongside crops and take the water, nutrients, sunlight and space the crops need, so crop growth and yield fall.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Which of the following is a common weed on Nigerian farms?
questions.explanation: Spear grass (Imperata) spreads by rhizomes and is a troublesome weed; maize, cowpea and cassava are crops.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Chemicals used to kill insect pests are called
questions.explanation: Insecticides kill insects; herbicides kill weeds, fungicides kill fungi and fertilizers supply nutrients.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Which pest commonly bores into stored beans and maize grains?
questions.explanation: Weevils lay eggs in stored grains and their larvae feed inside, leaving holes and powder.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Weed seeds can remain alive in the soil for many years and germinate only when conditions become favourable. This feature is called
questions.explanation: Dormancy is the resting state of seeds; long dormancy allows weed seeds to survive in the soil until conditions are good for germination.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Removing weeds by hand or with hoes and cutlasses is called
questions.explanation: Using hands, hoes and cutlasses to remove weeds is a physical or manual method because no chemicals or living organisms are used.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Using ladybird beetles to feed on aphids in a farm is an example of
questions.explanation: Biological control uses natural enemies, such as predators like ladybirds, to reduce pest populations.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Planting a cover crop such as Centrosema to smother weeds on a farm is an example of
questions.explanation: Cultural control uses good farm practices such as cover cropping, mulching and correct spacing to prevent weeds from growing.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Burning weeds on farmland as a method of weed control affects the soil by
options: destroying organic matter and useful soil organisms
adding more earthworms to the soil
increasing the water-holding capacity of the soil
making the soil less likely to erode
questions.explanation: Fire burns up dead plant matter and kills soil organisms, so the soil loses humus and becomes more open to erosion.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Cassava mealybugs damage cassava plants mainly by
options: biting and chewing the leaves into holes
boring tunnels into the woody stems
piercing the plant tissues and sucking the sap
questions.explanation: Mealybugs have piercing and sucking mouthparts; they suck sap from shoots and leaves, causing stunting and leaf distortion.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: The fall armyworm, a serious pest of maize, is classified as a
questions.explanation: The armyworm caterpillar has strong mandibles that bite and chew maize leaves and cobs.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Quelea birds are serious pests of
options: millet, sorghum and rice in northern Nigeria
cocoa pods in the forest zone
questions.explanation: Large flocks of quelea birds feed on ripening grains of millet, sorghum and rice, causing heavy losses in the north.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Traps and rodenticides are used mainly to control
questions.explanation: Rodenticides are poisons for rodents, and traps catch rats and grasscutters that damage crops and stored produce.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Aphids feeding on cowpea leaves can cause
options: leaf curling and the spread of viral diseases
questions.explanation: Aphids suck sap, which makes leaves curl and weakens the plant, and they carry viruses from diseased plants to healthy ones.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: A farmer sprayed herbicide on a windy day and the spray drifted onto a nearby grazing field. The MOST likely effect is that
options: the soil will become more fertile
the animals will produce more milk
livestock grazing there may be poisoned
questions.explanation: Herbicide drift contaminates pasture; animals that eat the treated grass can be poisoned, which is one harmful effect of chemical weed control.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Which statement BEST explains how pests reduce a farmer's income?
options: They make produce more attractive to buyers
They increase the amount of produce harvested
They reduce the cost of production
They lower both the quantity and the quality of produce, so less is sold at lower prices
questions.explanation: Pest damage leaves fewer crops to sell, and damaged produce fetches a lower price, so income falls.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Combining resistant crop varieties, crop rotation and careful use of pesticides only when necessary is called
questions.explanation: Integrated pest management combines several methods to keep pests low while reducing the harm of heavy chemical use.

questions.stem: Money used to start and run a farm business is called
questions.explanation: Capital includes money and man-made goods such as tools and machines used for production.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of land as a factor of agricultural production?
options: A worker hired to weed the farm
A plot of fertile soil on which crops are grown
questions.explanation: Land includes the soil and all natural resources used for farming.

questions.stem: The reward paid for the use of land is called
questions.explanation: Rent is the payment for land, wages for labour, interest for capital and profit for the entrepreneur.

questions.stem: The reward for the farmer who takes the risks and organises the other factors of production is
questions.explanation: The entrepreneur or manager bears the risks of the business and is rewarded with profit.

questions.stem: Labour supplied free of charge by the farmer's wife and children is called
questions.explanation: Family labour comes from members of the farmer's household and is usually unpaid.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a source of capital for a small-scale farmer?
options: A loan from a cooperative society
questions.explanation: Cooperative societies and banks such as the Bank of Agriculture lend money to farmers, providing capital.

questions.stem: A farmer in Kano grows tomatoes in the dry season by channelling water from a dam to the farm. This practice is called
questions.explanation: Irrigation is the artificial supply of water to crops, which allows farming in the dry season.

questions.stem: A farmer hires 6 labourers for 5 days and pays each ₦2,500 per day. What is the total wage bill?
questions.explanation: Total wage = 6 workers x 5 days x ₦2,500 = ₦75,000.

questions.stem: Which factor of agricultural production is MOST affected when many young people leave villages to look for jobs in cities?
questions.explanation: Rural-urban migration takes away able-bodied workers, reducing the labour available on farms.

questions.stem: A farmer has fertile land, workers and money, but his crops fail because planting was done late and inputs were wasted. Which factor of production was poorly handled?
questions.explanation: Management is planning and controlling the use of the other factors; poor timing and wastage show poor management.

questions.stem: A structure built for raising fish is called a
questions.explanation: Fish are kept in ponds, which may be earthen or concrete.

questions.stem: A fenced enclosure in which cattle are kept, especially at night, is called a
questions.explanation: A kraal is an enclosure for cattle; a hutch is for rabbits and a sty for pigs.

questions.stem: A fence on a farm is used mainly to
options: keep animals in and keep intruders out
questions.explanation: Fences mark the farm boundary, prevent livestock from straying and keep out thieves and stray animals.

questions.stem: Which farm building is used for keeping tractors and other farm machines?
questions.explanation: A machinery shed shelters tractors and implements from sun and rain, so they last longer.

questions.stem: A narrow structure with wire-mesh sides used for drying and storing maize cobs is called a
questions.explanation: The wire-mesh sides of a crib let air pass through so the maize cobs dry well and do not go mouldy.

questions.stem: The poultry housing system in which birds are kept in wire cages, one or a few birds per cage, is called the
questions.explanation: In the battery cage system, birds live in rows of wire cages, which makes egg collection and disease control easier.

questions.stem: A farm building where tools, fertilizers and chemicals are kept safely is called a
questions.explanation: A farm store protects tools and farm inputs from theft, rain and children.

questions.stem: Wooden poles of farm structures are often treated with a preservative such as creosote in order to
questions.explanation: Wood preservatives protect wood from termites and decay, so the structure lasts longer.

questions.stem: Why should the roof of a storage barn be inspected and repaired before the rains start?
options: To make the barn look new
To prevent rain from wetting and spoiling the stored produce
To allow rats to leave the barn
To reduce the weight of the roof
questions.explanation: A leaking roof lets water in, causing moulds and rotting of stored grains, so roofs should be repaired before the rainy season.

questions.stem: Which of the following is good maintenance of a fish pond?
options: Allowing the inlet and outlet pipes to block
Draining industrial waste into the pond
Clearing weeds and repairing leaking dykes
Pouring used engine oil into the pond
questions.explanation: Removing weeds and repairing leaks keep the water clean and at the right level, which keeps the fish healthy.

questions.stem: Which feature is MOST important in a poultry house built in a hot part of Nigeria?
options: A dark interior with no openings
questions.explanation: Good airflow removes heat, moisture and ammonia from droppings, preventing heat stress and disease in the birds.

questions.stem: A poultry house is usually sited some distance from the farmer's living house mainly to
options: reduce the spread of bad smell and diseases to people
increase the noise near the house
expose the birds to more thieves
make feeding the birds more difficult
questions.explanation: Keeping animal houses away from homes reduces odour, flies and the risk of diseases spreading to the family.

questions.stem: Propagation of crops using stems, roots, leaves or tubers is called
questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation uses parts of the plant other than seeds and does not involve the joining of sex cells.

questions.stem: Which of the following crops is commonly grown from seed?
questions.explanation: Maize is planted from grains (seeds), while sugarcane, cassava and plantain are propagated vegetatively.

questions.stem: Cocoyam is commonly propagated using
questions.explanation: Cocoyam produces small cormels around the main corm, and these are planted to grow new plants.

questions.stem: Pineapple is commonly propagated using
questions.explanation: Pineapple farmers plant the leafy crown on top of the fruit, slips from below the fruit or suckers from the stem.

questions.stem: Sweet potato is usually propagated by
questions.explanation: Pieces of sweet potato vines planted in ridges root quickly and produce new plants.

questions.stem: Ginger is propagated using its
questions.explanation: Ginger is planted from pieces of its underground stem (rhizome), each carrying buds.

questions.stem: In grafting, the part of the plant that provides the root system is called the
questions.explanation: The stock (rootstock) is the rooted part, while the scion is the shoot from the desired plant joined onto it.

questions.stem: Joining a bud from a high-yielding orange tree onto a rootstock is called
questions.explanation: Budding is a type of grafting that uses a single bud from the desired variety; it is common in citrus and rubber.

questions.stem: In layering, a branch is made to form roots while it is
options: cut off and dried in the sun
still attached to the parent plant
questions.explanation: In layering, a branch is bent and covered with soil while still attached, so it is fed by the parent until it forms roots.

questions.stem: One advantage of propagating crops by seed is that seeds
options: always produce plants exactly like the parent
are easy to store and transport
produce plants that fruit faster than cuttings
questions.explanation: Seeds are small, light and can be stored for long, so they are easy to handle and transport.

questions.stem: Removing a ring of bark from a branch, covering the cut with moist soil wrapped in polythene until roots form, and then cutting off the branch is called
questions.explanation: In marcotting, roots develop on the branch in the air while it is still on the parent plant.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of using yam setts instead of seeds for planting is that setts
options: are bulky and difficult to store for long
questions.explanation: Yam setts are large and heavy, so they take up much space, are costly to transport and can rot in storage.

questions.stem: Which is an advantage of propagating oranges by budding rather than by seed?
options: The trees never need any care
The trees live for only one season
The fruits will be different from the parent's
The trees fruit earlier and the fruits are like those of the parent
questions.explanation: Budded trees carry the desired variety, so they produce true-to-type fruits and begin fruiting earlier than seedlings.

questions.stem: Removing the stumps and roots of trees from cleared land is called
questions.explanation: Stumping is the removal of stumps and roots after clearing so that tillage and planting are easier.

questions.stem: Ploughing, harrowing and ridging are examples of
questions.explanation: Tillage means working the soil to prepare a good seedbed; ploughing, harrowing and ridging are tillage operations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a pre-planting operation?
questions.explanation: Clearing is done before planting; harvesting, thinning and storage are done after planting.

questions.stem: Animal dung, compost and green manure are examples of
questions.explanation: Organic manures come from plant and animal materials and improve soil fertility and structure.

questions.stem: Gathering mature crops from the farm is called
questions.explanation: Harvesting is the collection of crops when they are mature, at the end of the growing season.

questions.stem: Which of the following should a farmer look for when choosing a farm site?
options: Fertile, well-drained soil near water and a good road
Land that is waterlogged all year
Land far from any road or market
questions.explanation: Fertile, well-drained soil gives good crops, while nearness to water and roads makes irrigation and transport easier.

questions.stem: Dividing a cleared farmland into smaller units or beds for planting is called
questions.explanation: Plotting means marking out the land into plots or beds, which makes planting and management easier.

questions.stem: A good seed for planting should be
options: viable, healthy and free from pest damage
questions.explanation: Viable, healthy, undamaged seeds germinate well and grow into strong plants.

questions.stem: Correct spacing of crops on the farm helps to
options: reduce competition among plants for water, light and nutrients
questions.explanation: Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and resources and allows air movement, which lowers disease.

questions.stem: Moving seedlings from the nursery to the permanent field is called
questions.explanation: Transplanting is carefully lifting seedlings from the nursery and planting them in the field.

questions.stem: Nursery beds are usually provided with shade in order to
options: make the seedlings grow in darkness
keep away all air from the seedlings
protect young seedlings from strong sun and heavy rain
questions.explanation: Young seedlings are tender, and shade protects them from scorching sun and from damage by heavy raindrops.

questions.stem: In NPK 15:15:15 fertilizer, the letter K stands for
questions.explanation: N is nitrogen, P is phosphorus and K is potassium (from the Latin name kalium).

questions.stem: Applying fertilizer in a circle around each plant is called the
questions.explanation: In ring application, fertilizer is placed in a circle around the base of the plant, away from the stem.

questions.stem: If dry cowpea or soya bean pods are left on the farm long after they mature, the pods may
options: split open and scatter the seeds
questions.explanation: Delayed harvesting causes mature dry pods to shatter, so seeds are lost, which reduces yield.

questions.stem: Drying maize grains well before storage mainly helps to
options: make the grains germinate in the store
questions.explanation: Moist grains encourage moulds and heating in storage; well-dried grains keep longer.

questions.stem: Palm fruits are processed to give
questions.explanation: Pressing the palm fruit pulp yields palm oil, and the nuts are cracked to obtain palm kernels.

questions.stem: A farmer plants yam setts at a spacing of 1 m by 1 m on a field of 0.5 hectare. How many setts does he need? (1 hectare = 10,000 square metres)
questions.explanation: 0.5 hectare = 5,000 square metres; each sett occupies 1 square metre, so 5,000 setts are needed.

questions.stem: How many kilograms of nitrogen are contained in a 50 kg bag of NPK 20:10:10 fertilizer?
questions.explanation: The fertilizer is 20% nitrogen, so 20/100 x 50 kg = 10 kg of nitrogen.

questions.stem: Gradually reducing watering and exposing nursery seedlings to full sunlight before transplanting is called
questions.explanation: Hardening off toughens seedlings so they can survive the harsher conditions of the field after transplanting.

questions.stem: Dry cowpea grains stored in airtight triple-layer bags are protected from weevils mainly because
options: the insects die from lack of oxygen
the grains become wet inside the bags
questions.explanation: Airtight bags cut off the air supply, so weevils inside cannot breathe and die without the use of chemicals.

questions.stem: After harvesting cocoa pods, the beans are fermented before drying mainly to
options: develop the chocolate flavour and colour
questions.explanation: Fermentation removes the pulp and starts chemical changes in the bean that produce the flavour and brown colour needed for good chocolate.

questions.stem: Feeds that mainly supply animals with energy are called
questions.explanation: Energy feeds such as maize and cassava are rich in carbohydrates and fats, which provide energy.

questions.stem: A container used for supplying feed to poultry is called a
questions.explanation: A feeder holds feed for the birds, while a drinker holds water.

questions.stem: Feeds with high fibre content, such as hay and fresh grass, are called
questions.explanation: Roughages are bulky and high in fibre; they are the main feed of ruminants.

questions.stem: Grass cut and dried for feeding animals in the dry season is called
questions.explanation: Hay is grass or legume fodder that has been cut and dried so that it can be stored.

questions.stem: A block containing salts and minerals that cattle lick is called a
questions.explanation: A salt lick supplies minerals such as sodium and calcium that animals need.

questions.stem: A feed containing all the nutrients an animal needs in the right proportions is called a
questions.explanation: A balanced ration supplies carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals and water in the correct amounts.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a protein feed of plant origin?
questions.explanation: Soybean meal comes from a plant and is rich in protein; blood meal is from animals, while maize bran and cassava peels mainly provide energy.

questions.stem: Oyster shell and bone meal are added to the feed of laying hens mainly to supply
questions.explanation: Eggshells are made largely of calcium carbonate, so layers need extra calcium from oyster shell or bone meal.

questions.stem: Animals should be given clean water every day mainly because water
options: is needed for digestion, body cooling and other body functions
questions.explanation: Water is needed for digestion, transport of nutrients, removal of waste and control of body temperature.

questions.stem: Green grass stored in a moist state in a pit or silo, where it ferments and keeps for dry season feeding, is called
questions.explanation: Silage is fodder preserved by fermentation in airtight conditions, so it stays moist and nutritious.

questions.stem: Cattle can live well on grass but chickens cannot, mainly because cattle
options: have micro-organisms in the rumen that digest fibre
questions.explanation: The rumen contains bacteria that break down cellulose in grass; chickens lack this, so they need concentrates.

questions.stem: A feed mix of 120 kg contains 30 kg of soybean meal. What percentage of the mix is soybean meal?
questions.explanation: Percentage = 30/120 x 100 = 25%.

questions.stem: Insects such as tsetse flies that carry disease organisms from one animal to another are called
questions.explanation: A vector carries disease-causing organisms from infected animals to healthy ones.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an external parasite of farm animals?
questions.explanation: Ticks live on the skin and suck blood, so they are external parasites; the others live inside the body.

questions.stem: Which sanitation practice helps to prevent disease in a poultry house?
options: Removing wet litter and disinfecting the house
Leaving dead birds in the pen
questions.explanation: Wet litter and dirt allow germs to multiply; clean, dry litter and disinfection reduce disease.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a sign of a healthy farm animal?
questions.explanation: A healthy animal is active and alert with bright eyes, a smooth coat and normal droppings.

questions.stem: Anthrax in cattle is caused by a
questions.explanation: Anthrax is a serious bacterial disease that can also infect humans.

questions.stem: Foot and mouth disease of cattle is caused by a
questions.explanation: Foot and mouth disease is a highly contagious viral disease causing blisters in the mouth and on the feet.

questions.stem: Tapeworm and roundworm infestations in goats are controlled mainly by
questions.explanation: Anthelmintics (dewormers) kill internal worms in the gut.

questions.stem: Ticks on cattle are best controlled by
options: dipping or spraying the animals with acaricides
keeping the animals in the sun
questions.explanation: Acaricides kill ticks on the skin, and dipping or spraying applies them over the whole body.

questions.stem: Animals that drink from a trough used by sick animals can become infected. This is disease transmission through
questions.explanation: Germs from sick animals pass into shared water and feed, which then infect healthy animals.

questions.stem: Animals that die of a contagious disease should be
questions.explanation: Burning or deep burial destroys the germs and prevents spread to other animals and people.

questions.stem: Separating sick animals from the healthy ones in a herd is called
questions.explanation: Isolation keeps sick animals apart so the disease does not spread to the healthy animals.

questions.stem: Mastitis is a disease that affects the
questions.explanation: Mastitis is an inflammation of the udder, usually caused by bacteria, which reduces milk yield and quality.

questions.stem: Dogs kept on the farm should be vaccinated regularly against
questions.explanation: Rabies is a deadly viral disease spread by bites from infected animals, so dogs must be vaccinated to protect people and other animals.

questions.stem: Vaccines are given to healthy animals in order to
options: cure animals that are already very sick
build immunity before they are exposed to the disease
questions.explanation: Vaccination prepares the animal's body to fight a disease before infection, so it prevents rather than cures disease.

questions.stem: Scab-like, wart-like sores on the comb and wattles of chickens are a symptom of
questions.explanation: Fowl pox is a viral disease that causes wart-like lesions on the unfeathered parts of birds such as the comb and wattles.

questions.stem: A farmer's goats eat well but are losing weight, have rough coats, pale gums and swollen bellies. The MOST likely cause is
questions.explanation: Internal worms feed on blood and nutrients, causing weight loss, anaemia (pale gums), rough coat and pot belly.

questions.stem: Control of liver fluke in cattle includes the control of water snails because the snails
options: drink the water meant for cattle
are the intermediate hosts of the fluke
questions.explanation: The liver fluke completes part of its life cycle in water snails, so reducing snails breaks the cycle.

questions.stem: Which of the following fish lives in salt water (the sea)?
questions.explanation: Sardines are marine fish; tilapia, catfish and carp are freshwater fish.

questions.stem: Fish obtain oxygen from water using their
questions.explanation: Gills absorb dissolved oxygen from water as it passes over them.

questions.stem: A fishing net thrown by hand that spreads out and sinks over fish is called a
questions.explanation: The weighted edge of a cast net makes it sink and close over fish.

questions.stem: Fishermen in riverine areas commonly preserve their catch by
options: leaving it in the sun with flies
questions.explanation: Smoking removes moisture and adds substances that slow spoilage, so smoked fish keeps for weeks.

questions.stem: Fish whose skeletons are made of bone, such as tilapia, are called
questions.explanation: Bony fish have skeletons of true bone, unlike sharks and rays whose skeletons are cartilage.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a cartilaginous fish?
questions.explanation: Rays and sharks have skeletons made of cartilage; tilapia, catfish and mackerel are bony fish.

questions.stem: Large fishing boats that drag nets along the sea to catch fish are using a method called
questions.explanation: Trawling uses a large bag-shaped net pulled by a boat to catch many fish at once.

questions.stem: Fish liver oil is valued mainly as a source of
questions.explanation: Fish liver oils are rich in vitamins A and D, which are needed for good eyesight and strong bones.

questions.stem: Young fish used for stocking a fish pond are called
questions.explanation: Fingerlings are small young fish bought from hatcheries and stocked into ponds to grow to table size.

questions.stem: Oil spillage in the creeks of the Niger Delta affects fishing mainly by
options: improving the quality of the water
killing fish and destroying their breeding grounds
questions.explanation: Crude oil covers the water, cuts off oxygen and poisons fish and their eggs, so catches fall.

questions.stem: Using fishing nets with very small mesh is discouraged mainly because such nets
options: catch young fish and reduce future fish stock
questions.explanation: Small-mesh nets trap juvenile fish before they can breed, which reduces the number of fish in future.

questions.stem: Oysters and periwinkles are aquatic organisms classified as
questions.explanation: Oysters and periwinkles are soft-bodied animals with shells, which are molluscs; crabs and shrimps are crustaceans.

questions.stem: A farmer harvested 250 kg of catfish from his pond and sold it at ₦1,800 per kg. How much did he receive?
Wild animals living in a forest are called
questions.explanation: Wildlife refers to undomesticated animals living in their natural habitats such as forests.

questions.stem: Which forest product is widely used as cooking fuel in Nigerian homes?
questions.explanation: Firewood and charcoal from trees are major cooking fuels in many Nigerian homes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a Nigerian timber tree?
questions.explanation: Iroko is a hardwood tree from Nigerian forests used for furniture and building; the others are grasses.

questions.stem: Ogbono (bush mango) seeds used in soup are an example of forest
questions.explanation: Forests provide edible fruits and seeds such as bush mango, African star apple and kola.

questions.stem: Leaves, roots and barks collected from the forest for treating illnesses are called
questions.explanation: Many forest plants contain substances used as medicine, so they are collected as medicinal herbs.

questions.stem: Forests help the environment by
options: absorbing carbon dioxide and releasing oxygen
questions.explanation: Trees use carbon dioxide in photosynthesis and release oxygen, which helps to keep the air clean and the climate stable.

questions.stem: Rows of trees planted around a farm to reduce the speed of wind are called
questions.explanation: Windbreaks slow down wind, protecting crops and soil from wind damage and erosion.

questions.stem: An area of forest protected by law from farming, logging and hunting is called a
questions.explanation: Forest reserves such as Omo Forest Reserve are protected areas set aside to conserve trees and wildlife.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a way of conserving wildlife in Nigeria?
options: Setting up game reserves and national parks such as Yankari
Burning the bush every dry season
Hunting animals at all times of the year
questions.explanation: Game reserves and national parks protect wild animals and their habitats from hunting and destruction.

questions.stem: Forests provide wild animals with
questions.explanation: Trees and undergrowth give wild animals places to live, hide and breed, and provide fruits, leaves and prey for food.

questions.stem: Growing food crops between young forest trees until the tree canopy closes is called the
questions.explanation: In the taungya system, farmers grow crops among young trees, so food is produced while the forest is re-established.

questions.stem: Which is a likely effect of large-scale deforestation in northern Nigeria?
options: An increase in the number of wild animals
questions.explanation: Removing trees exposes the soil to wind and sun, which leads to soil loss and the southward spread of desert conditions.

questions.stem: Which of the following human activities is a major cause of forest loss in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Clearing forest land for farming is a major cause of forest loss, while the other options help to keep or restore forests.

questions.stem: Grains such as rice and maize are usually packaged for sale in
questions.explanation: Sacks are cheap, strong and suitable for dry, solid, free-flowing produce such as grains.

questions.stem: Garri and flour sold in small quantities in the market are commonly packed in
questions.explanation: Polythene bags are light and cheap, and they keep dry powdered or granular produce clean.

questions.stem: One importance of packaging farm produce is that it
options: reduces the quality of the produce
protects the produce from damage and contamination
questions.explanation: Good packaging keeps produce clean, prevents damage and makes handling, transport and storage easier.

questions.stem: Tomatoes are packed in shallow crates rather than in large heavy sacks mainly to
questions.explanation: Tomatoes are soft; shallow, rigid crates stop the weight of produce on top from crushing the fruits at the bottom.

questions.stem: When choosing packaging for live goats being taken to market, the MOST important requirement is
questions.explanation: Live animals need air and room to stand, so their transport must be well ventilated and not overcrowded.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST suitable package for honey?
options: A clean, sealed glass jar or bottle
questions.explanation: Honey is a liquid, so it needs a clean, sealed container that will not leak.

questions.stem: The packaging criterion considered when deciding to use large bales or big containers for a large quantity of produce is
questions.explanation: Bulkiness refers to the size or volume of produce; bulky produce needs large packages such as bales.

questions.stem: Information such as the weight, date of packaging and name of the producer printed on a package of farm produce is called the
questions.explanation: A label gives buyers information about the product and the producer and helps to promote the produce.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a medium for advertising farm produce?
questions.explanation: Radio jingles are announcements that inform listeners about a product, so radio is a medium of advertising.

questions.stem: One benefit of advertising farm produce is that it
options: reduces the quality of the produce
questions.explanation: Advertising makes people aware of the produce, where to get it and its price, which increases sales.

questions.stem: During festive periods such as Christmas and Sallah, the price of live chickens and rams usually rises because
questions.explanation: When many people want to buy at the same time and supply does not increase as fast, prices rise.

questions.stem: The price at which a product is usually sold in a particular market at a given time is called the
questions.explanation: Market price is the price at which buyers and sellers are trading a product at a given time and place.

questions.stem: A farmer sells maize at a lower price per bag to a buyer who takes 100 bags. This shows that price can be affected by the
questions.explanation: Buyers who purchase large quantities are often given a lower price per unit, so quantity affects price.

questions.stem: It cost a farmer ₦900,000 to produce 300 crates of eggs. What is the cost of producing one crate?
Giving free samples of honey to visitors at an agricultural show to attract buyers is a form of
questions.explanation: Sales promotion uses activities such as free samples, discounts and displays to encourage people to buy.

questions.stem: A farmer who uses irrigation to produce tomatoes in the dry season is likely to
options: sell at a higher price because supply is low at that time
be unable to sell the tomatoes
sell at a lower price because supply is high
questions.explanation: In the dry season few farmers produce tomatoes, so supply is low and prices are high for those who produce then.

questions.stem: A farmer spent ₦40,000 to produce 20 bags of pepper and sold each bag at ₦2,600. What was his profit?
A record showing the number of eggs collected each day on a poultry farm is a
questions.explanation: A production record shows the quantity of produce (eggs, milk, crops) obtained over time.

questions.stem: A record of items bought for use on the farm, such as seeds, fertilizer and feed, is called an
questions.explanation: An input record lists the materials bought and used in production, with quantities and costs.

questions.stem: A record showing how much farm produce was used by the farmer's household is called a
questions.explanation: A consumption record tracks produce used at home, which is important for knowing the true value of production.

questions.stem: A record that shows the dates, quantities, prices and buyers of produce sold is called a
questions.explanation: A sales record shows all the produce sold, to whom, and for how much.

questions.stem: The document a farmer receives from a supplier showing feed bought on credit and the amount owed is the
questions.explanation: A purchase invoice is sent by the seller to the buyer; from the farmer's point of view, it records goods bought on credit.

questions.stem: Feed that a farmer returns to the supplier because it was damaged is recorded in the
questions.explanation: Goods sent back by the business to its supplier are returns outwards.

questions.stem: Credit purchases of fertilizer by a farmer are first recorded in the
questions.explanation: The purchases journal (day book) records goods bought on credit for resale or use in the business.

questions.stem: The sales journal is used to record
questions.explanation: The sales journal lists goods sold on credit, taken from copies of sales invoices.

questions.stem: Which computer program is MOST suitable for keeping farm records and calculating totals automatically?
questions.explanation: A spreadsheet arranges data in rows and columns and calculates totals using formulas, which suits farm records.

questions.stem: A farm had total sales of ₦850,000 and total expenses of ₦620,000 in a year. What was the net profit?
questions.explanation: Net profit = total sales - total expenses = ₦850,000 - ₦620,000 = ₦230,000.

questions.stem: Source documents such as invoices and receipts are important in book keeping because they
options: provide evidence of transactions for making entries in the books
replace the need for any records
questions.explanation: Entries in journals and ledgers are made from source documents, which prove that the transactions took place.

questions.stem: A poultry farm had sales of ₦300,000 and expenses of ₦345,000 in a month. What was the result?
questions.explanation: Expenses exceeded sales: ₦345,000 - ₦300,000 = ₦45,000, so the farm made a loss of ₦45,000.

questions.stem: A farm inventory lists 3 wheelbarrows at ₦25,000 each and 10 hoes at ₦3,500 each. What is the total value of these items?
Good farm records can help a farmer to obtain a bank loan mainly because they
options: replace the need for collateral and repayment
show the bank how the farm has performed
guarantee that crops will never fail
questions.explanation: Banks want evidence of income and expenses, and records show that the farm is managed well enough to repay a loan.

questions.stem: A person who owns shares in a company is called a
questions.explanation: A shareholder is a part-owner of a company through the shares he or she has bought.

questions.stem: Which group of people takes part in buying and selling on the stock exchange?
questions.explanation: The stock exchange brings together people who want to buy shares and people who want to sell them, often through brokers.

questions.stem: The part of a company's profit paid to its shareholders is called a
questions.explanation: Companies share part of their profit with shareholders as dividends, according to the number of shares held.

questions.stem: Persons who act on behalf of farmers to sell their produce or commodities to buyers are called
questions.explanation: Farmers' agents represent farmers in markets and exchanges and help them find buyers for their produce.

questions.stem: An agro-allied company such as a feed mill can raise money to expand through the stock exchange by
questions.explanation: Selling shares brings in capital from investors, which the company uses to grow its business.

questions.stem: An organised market where agricultural commodities such as maize, cocoa and sesame are bought and sold in standard grades is called a
questions.explanation: A commodity exchange, such as the Nigeria Commodity Exchange, trades agricultural produce in agreed grades and quantities.

questions.stem: A shareholder owns 2,000 shares in a palm oil company that pays a dividend of ₦1.50 per share. How much dividend does she receive?
questions.explanation: Dividend = 2,000 shares x ₦1.50 = ₦3,000.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a Nigerian agricultural export produce?
questions.explanation: Sesame is grown in states such as Nasarawa, Benue and Jigawa and exported; crude oil is a mineral, not farm produce.

questions.stem: Agricultural trade fairs abroad help Nigerian farmers and exporters mainly to
options: reduce the quality of their produce
find foreign buyers for their produce
questions.explanation: Trade fairs show Nigerian produce to foreign buyers, opening new export markets.

questions.stem: Which list contains ONLY agricultural export produce of Nigeria?
options: Crude oil, cocoa, tin and cars
Cocoa, crude oil, ginger and cars
Tin, coal, crude oil and limestone
questions.explanation: Cocoa, cashew, ginger and sesame are farm produce exported from Nigeria; crude oil, tin, coal and limestone are minerals.

questions.stem: Nigerian farm produce must meet quality standards before export mainly to
options: make the produce cheaper to grow
questions.explanation: Foreign markets reject produce that is dirty, poorly graded or contains harmful residues, so meeting standards keeps the market open.

questions.stem: A cooperative exports 5 tonnes of dried ginger at 1,200 US dollars per tonne. How much does it earn?
questions.explanation: Earnings = 5 tonnes x 1,200 US dollars = 6,000 US dollars, which is foreign exchange for Nigeria.

questions.stem: The agency that inspects and certifies plants and agricultural produce leaving Nigeria to make sure they are free from pests and diseases is the
questions.explanation: NAQS carries out inspection and quarantine checks and issues certificates for agricultural exports and imports.

questions.stem: Which of the following can limit Nigeria's agricultural exports?
options: Poor quality produce and high pesticide residues
Proper drying and grading of produce
questions.explanation: Produce that is poorly handled or contains too much chemical residue is rejected abroad, which reduces exports.

questions.stem: Exporting processed cassava products such as starch and flour instead of raw cassava benefits Nigeria because
options: it reduces jobs in the country
processing adds value, so the products earn more money
raw cassava cannot be grown in Nigeria
questions.explanation: Processing increases the value of the produce, creates jobs and earns more foreign exchange than selling raw tubers.

questions.stem:
(a) What is agriculture? [2 marks]
(b) State four importance of agriculture to Nigeria. [4 marks]
(c) Name four forms of agricultural activities practised in Nigerian communities. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Agriculture is the cultivation of crops and the rearing of animals (and fish) for the use of man.
1 mark: (b) Provides food for the population
1 mark: (b) Provides raw materials for industries (e.g. cotton, cocoa, oil palm)
1 mark: (b) Provides employment / income
1 mark: (b) Earns foreign exchange through exports (accept: provides shelter or clothing materials)
1 mark: (c) Growing of crops (crop production)
1 mark: (c) Rearing of livestock (e.g. poultry, goats, cattle)
1 mark: (c) Fish farming (aquaculture)
1 mark: (c) Bee keeping (apiculture) or snail rearing (heliciculture)
questions.explanation: Agriculture covers crop and animal production. It feeds the nation, supplies industries, creates jobs and earns foreign exchange, and is practised as crop farming, livestock rearing, fish farming, bee keeping and snail rearing.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous crops, giving TWO examples of each. [6 marks]
(b) Classify the following crops according to their main nutrient: cassava, cowpea, oil palm, orange. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Monocots have one seed leaf (cotyledon), parallel leaf veins and fibrous roots
1 mark: (a) Two examples of monocots, e.g. maize, rice, guinea corn, millet
2 marks: (a) Dicots have two seed leaves, net-veined leaves and usually a taproot
1 mark: (a) Two examples of dicots, e.g. cowpea, melon, groundnut, soya bean
1 mark: (b) Cassava: carbohydrate
1 mark: (b) Cowpea: protein
1 mark: (b) Oil palm: fats and oil
1 mark: (b) Orange: vitamins and minerals
questions.explanation: Monocots and dicots differ in number of cotyledons, leaf venation and root type. Crops can also be grouped by the main food nutrient they supply.

questions.topic: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals
questions.stem:
(a) Define a ruminant animal and give TWO examples. [3 marks]
(b) State three differences between a ruminant and a monogastric animal. [3 marks]
(c) Name one farm animal kept for each of the following uses: (i) work (ii) milk (iii) guarding the farm (iv) eggs. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) A ruminant is an animal with a four-chambered stomach that chews the cud
2 marks: (a) Any two examples, e.g. cattle, goat, sheep (1 mark each)
1 mark: (b) Ruminants have four stomach compartments; monogastrics have one simple stomach
1 mark: (b) Ruminants chew the cud; monogastrics do not
1 mark: (b) Ruminants digest much fibre (grass) with the help of rumen microbes; monogastrics need more concentrates
1 mark: (c)(i) Work: donkey, bullock, horse or camel
1 mark: (c)(ii) Milk: dairy cow or goat
1 mark: (c)(iii) Guarding: dog
1 mark: (c)(iv) Eggs: layers (chicken), duck or guinea fowl
questions.explanation: Ruminants such as cattle and goats have a complex stomach and chew the cud, unlike monogastric animals such as pigs and poultry. Farm animals are also grouped by use.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem:
(a) State three characteristics of weeds. [3 marks]
(b) Describe briefly three methods of controlling weeds on a farm. [3 marks]
(c) Classify insect pests according to their mouthparts and give ONE example of each class. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Produce many seeds
1 mark: (a) Seeds are easily dispersed (by wind, water, animals)
1 mark: (a) Seeds have long dormancy / weeds grow fast and are hardy (accept: compete strongly, spread by rhizomes)
1 mark: (b) Manual/physical control: hand pulling, hoeing or slashing
1 mark: (b) Chemical control: spraying herbicides
1 mark: (b) Cultural or biological control: mulching, cover crops, crop rotation, or use of natural enemies/grazing animals
1 mark: (c) Biting and chewing insects
1 mark: (c) Example, e.g. grasshopper, armyworm, termite, weevil
1 mark: (c) Piercing and sucking insects
1 mark: (c) Example, e.g. aphid, mealybug, cotton stainer
questions.explanation: Weeds are hardy and spread easily, so farmers use several control methods. Insect pests are grouped by mouthparts because this determines the type of damage and the control used.

questions.stem:
(a) Name four farm structures or buildings and state the use of each. [8 marks]
(b) State two ways of maintaining farm buildings. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) First structure named, e.g. poultry house
1 mark: (a) Its use, e.g. housing birds
1 mark: (a) Second structure, e.g. barn or crib
1 mark: (a) Its use, e.g. storing or drying grains
1 mark: (a) Third structure, e.g. fish pond
1 mark: (a) Its use, e.g. rearing fish
1 mark: (a) Fourth structure, e.g. farm store, hutch, sty, kraal or fence
1 mark: (a) Its correct use
1 mark: (b) Regular cleaning and disinfecting
1 mark: (b) Repairing damaged roofs, walls or fences / painting or treating wood against termites
questions.explanation: Farm structures shelter animals, store produce and protect inputs. Regular cleaning and repair keep them useful for a long time.

questions.stem:
(a) What is crop propagation? [2 marks]
(b) Name four vegetative organs used in propagating crops and give a crop propagated by each. [4 marks]
(c) State two advantages and two disadvantages of propagating crops by seed. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Crop propagation is the multiplication or reproduction of crop plants, by seed or vegetative parts
1 mark: (b) Stem cuttings: cassava or sugarcane
1 mark: (b) Tubers/setts: yam
1 mark: (b) Suckers: plantain, banana or pineapple
1 mark: (b) Any other, e.g. rhizome: ginger; corm/cormel: cocoyam; vine: sweet potato
1 mark: (c) Advantage: seeds are easy to store and transport
1 mark: (c) Advantage: many plants produced cheaply / possible to develop new varieties
1 mark: (c) Disadvantage: offspring may differ from the parent
1 mark: (c) Disadvantage: some seeds have dormancy or low viability / plants take longer to mature
questions.explanation: Propagation can be sexual (seed) or asexual (vegetative). Each has advantages and disadvantages for the farmer.

questions.stem:
(a) List four pre-planting operations. [4 marks]
(b) Explain the following post-planting operations: (i) thinning (ii) supplying (iii) mulching. [6 marks]
(c) State two effects of late harvesting of crops. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Choice of site
1 mark: (a) Clearing
1 mark: (a) Stumping or tillage (ploughing, harrowing, ridging)
1 mark: (a) Seed selection or nursery preparation (accept plotting)
2 marks: (b)(i) Thinning: removing excess seedlings from a stand so that the remaining ones grow well
2 marks: (b)(ii) Supplying: replacing seeds or seedlings that failed to germinate or died
2 marks: (b)(iii) Mulching: covering the soil around crops with dry grass, leaves or other materials to conserve moisture and suppress weeds
1 mark: (c) Losses to pests, birds, rodents and rain (shattering, sprouting, rotting)
1 mark: (c) Poor quality produce and lower market price
questions.explanation: Agricultural practices are carried out before, during and after planting. Timely harvesting protects both the quantity and quality of produce.

questions.stem:
(a) Name one example each of a bacterial, a viral, a protozoan and a fungal disease of farm animals. [4 marks]
(b) State four ways by which diseases are transmitted among farm animals. [4 marks]
(c) Describe four methods of preventing and controlling diseases on a livestock farm. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Bacterial: anthrax, mastitis, tuberculosis or brucellosis
1 mark: (a) Viral: Newcastle disease, foot and mouth disease, fowl pox or rabies
1 mark: (a) Protozoan: coccidiosis or trypanosomiasis
1 mark: (a) Fungal: ringworm or aspergillosis
1 mark: (b) Direct contact with infected animals
1 mark: (b) Contaminated feed and water
1 mark: (b) Vectors, e.g. tsetse flies and ticks
1 mark: (b) Discharges/droppings or contaminated equipment and air
1 mark: (c) Good sanitation: cleaning and disinfecting houses and equipment
1 mark: (c) Vaccination/medication (e.g. deworming, dipping)
1 mark: (c) Isolation of sick animals and quarantine of new stock
1 mark: (c) Proper disposal of dead animals by burning or deep burial
questions.explanation: Animal diseases are caused by different organisms and spread in several ways, so prevention combines hygiene, vaccination, isolation and proper disposal.

questions.stem:
(a) Define fishery. [2 marks]
(b) Classify fish based on (i) habitat (ii) morphology, giving ONE example of each class. [4 marks]
(c) State two methods of fishing and two risk factors in fish farming. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Fishery is the catching, rearing, processing and marketing of fish and other aquatic organisms
1 mark: (b)(i) Freshwater fish, e.g. tilapia or catfish
1 mark: (b)(i) Salt-water (marine) fish, e.g. sardine, mackerel or shark
1 mark: (b)(ii) Bony fish, e.g. tilapia
1 mark: (b)(ii) Cartilaginous fish, e.g. shark or ray
1 mark: (c) Method 1, e.g. hook and line, cast net, gill net, trap or trawling
1 mark: (c) Method 2 (different from the first)
1 mark: (c) Risk: pollution of water by chemicals or industrial effluents (oil spillage)
1 mark: (c) Risk: contamination of fish with chemicals used to catch fish (accept poor water quality, overstocking)
questions.explanation: Fish are grouped by where they live and by their skeleton. Fishing methods vary, and pollution and chemical misuse are major risks.

questions.stem:
(a) Name three types of forest found in Nigeria and describe one feature of each. [6 marks]
(b) State four human activities that affect the forest. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Mangrove (swamp) forest
1 mark: (a) Found in swampy, salty coastal areas such as the Niger Delta
1 mark: (a) Rain forest
1 mark: (a) Many tall trees and thick undergrowth with heavy rainfall
1 mark: (a) Derived forest (or savanna)
1 mark: (a) Few trees, developed after the original forest was cleared
1 mark: (b) Deforestation / clearing for farming or building
1 mark: (b) Logging of timber without replanting
1 mark: (b) Bush burning
1 mark: (b) Indiscriminate hunting (accept: fuelwood collection, mining)
questions.explanation: Nigeria has mangrove, rain and derived forests. Human activities such as clearing, logging, bush burning and hunting reduce forest cover and wildlife.

questions.stem:
Mr Danladi keeps 1,500 layers. In March he bought feed for ₦520,000, paid wages of ₦90,000 and spent ₦30,000 on drugs. He sold 1,000 crates of eggs at ₦2,800 per crate.
(a) What is a farm record? [2 marks]
(b) Calculate (i) his total expenses (ii) his total sales (iii) his profit or loss for March. [6 marks]
(c) Name four types of farm records he should keep. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) A farm record is a written account of the activities, inputs, outputs and transactions on a farm
2 marks: (b)(i) Total expenses = 520,000 + 90,000 + 30,000 = ₦640,000
2 marks: (b)(ii) Total sales = 1,000 x 2,800 = ₦2,800,000
2 marks: (b)(iii) Profit = 2,800,000 - 640,000 = ₦2,160,000
1 mark: (c) Production record (eggs collected)
1 mark: (c) Input record (feed, drugs)
1 mark: (c) Sales record
1 mark: (c) Farm diary, inventory, labour or profit and loss account
questions.explanation: Records show where money goes and what the farm earns. Expenses are added, sales are quantity x price, and profit is sales minus expenses.

questions.stem:
(a) What is pricing? [2 marks]
(b) State four factors that determine the price of farm produce. [4 marks]
(c) State four packaging criteria for farm produce. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Pricing is the process of fixing the price at which a product is sold
1 mark: (b) Cost of production
1 mark: (b) Quality of produce
1 mark: (b) Quantity of produce / forces of demand and supply
1 mark: (b) Market price or season of the produce
1 mark: (c) Nature of the produce (liquid or solid, shape)
1 mark: (c) Bulkiness (size)
1 mark: (c) Whether live, frozen or dry
1 mark: (c) Distance to the market
questions.explanation: Prices depend on cost, quality, quantity, demand and supply and season. Packaging is chosen according to the nature, size and condition of the produce and how far it will travel.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of export promotion. [2 marks]
(b) Name four agricultural produce exported from Nigeria. [4 marks]
(c) State two benefits of export promotion and two importance of the stock exchange to agriculture. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Export promotion is the encouragement by government and other bodies of the production and sale of local goods to other countries
1 mark: (b) Cocoa
1 mark: (b) Palm produce (palm kernel, palm oil)
1 mark: (b) Hides and skins
1 mark: (b) Any other, e.g. sesame, cashew, ginger, groundnut, cassava products, pepper
1 mark: (c) Export: earns foreign exchange
1 mark: (c) Export: provides additional markets and income for farmers
1 mark: (c) Stock exchange: encourages investment in agriculture
1 mark: (c) Stock exchange: encourages contract farming / helps agro-allied firms raise capital
questions.explanation: Export promotion helps Nigerian produce reach foreign markets, earning foreign exchange and income, while the stock exchange channels investment into agriculture.
